key_insight: A large-scale, temporally coherent dataset captured from AAA games using a novel dual-screen stitched capture method enables realistic, synchronized RGB + G-buffer training data for scaling generative inverse and forward rendering to real-world scenarios.
problem_solved: Existing synthetic datasets lack realism and temporal coherence, limiting the performance and generalization of generative inverse/forward rendering methods in real-world settings.
method: Dual-screen stitched capture pipeline to record synchronized visuals from high-fidelity game engines.
Curated 4M continuous frames at 720p/30 FPS with RGB plus five G-buffer channels (e.g., depth, normals, albedo, material/lighting maps) across diverse scenes, effects, and dynamic interactions.
Dataset curation prioritizing temporal continuity and visual complexity to bridge the synthetic→real domain gap for training and evaluation.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a high-fidelity, temporally coherent training and evaluation resource that improves realism, temporal stability, and generalization of neural rendering, inverse rendering, and related pipelines—reducing reliance on costly real-world capture.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the dual-screen stitched capture setup (two screens → stitched pipeline → synchronized RGB + G-buffers).
Side-by-side visual sample showing an RGB frame and the aligned five G-buffer channels.
Temporal strip / frame sequence illustrating continuity across consecutive frames (30 FPS).
Dataset statistics card (4M frames, resolution/FPS, counts of scene types/effects) as an easy-to-read infographic.
paper_authors: Zheng-Hui Huang, Zhixiang Wang, Jiaming Tan, Ruihan Yu, Yidan Zhang
